title: Save my history writes workout and exercise names into the spreadsheet file exactly as typed, so a name starting with = runs as a formula
what: Save my history puts each workout name, workout note, exercise name and exercise note into the spreadsheet file inside quotes, but does not neutralise text that starts with =, +, - or @. When the member opens that file in Excel or Google Sheets, such a cell is treated as a formula. Most of this text is the member's own, but exercise names also arrive from the gym's workout plans and from shared routine files, which create new exercises under whatever name the sender chose. A crafted name could show a misleading link or pull data into the sheet when opened.
expected: Any text cell that starts with =, +, - or @ is written so a spreadsheet shows it as plain text, while the file still imports back into Hevy, Strong and MettleUp.
who: members who save their history and open it in a spreadsheet app
how_often: only when a workout or exercise name starts with a formula sign
fix_line: Prefix text cells that start with a formula sign with a single quote when writing the file, and teach the importer to drop that quote.

items.reason: The area makes four server calls, all reads through the member's own secret gym key: member_gym_plans, member_gym_wod, member_measurements and member_diet_plans. Each runs as owner with a fixed search path, is open to anon and signed-in callers by design, and finds the gym only from the hashed member key (an unknown key is refused), then answers for that one gym and roster member. The Groq coach note goes to Groq with the member's own key, not to our server. Everything else works on the phone's own database.

Tables read behind these calls: crm_records (plans and memberships), gym_body_measurements, gym_diet_plans, gym_wods, gym_members. Apps cannot read any of them directly: row rules are on with no policies, and 0035 takes all rights from anon and signed-in users on the measurement and diet tables (its test 17 checks that). Cross-gym tests: workout plans test 8 (a member of another gym with the same number gets no plans); measurements test 6z and diet plans test 11z (other gym's member gets nothing); workout of the day tests 6e/6f; crm_records direct pull/push across gyms in the security test.
Rule applied: every server table this area reaches has a cross-gym test (listed under L3.2), so no finding.
Rule applied: no live cross-gym attempt was run; only the existing database tests were read.
The secrets scan has no key pattern hits in this area, and a search of the area's files finds no keys or tokens; the only web address is the Hevy documentation link in a comment.

The only paid-service key is the optional Groq key for the AI finish note. It is the member's own key, typed in Settings and kept in the phone's secure store; nothing ships inside the app, and no call is made unless the hidden coach switch, the member's coach-notes setting and a key are all present.
No sign-in, PIN, session or password handling in these workout services; the gym calls reuse the member key the shop area stores.

Every database query here binds the typed text as a parameter, and the history search escapes the member's own % and _ and caps the text at 60 characters. The fault found is in the spreadsheet export: text cells are quoted but not made formula-safe.

Nothing is uploaded to our server. Exercise photos and videos stay on the phone, with a 30-second and 80 MB cap on videos; photo backup goes only into Android's own backup, shrunk to a 15 MB budget; the Hevy and Strong file the member picks is read on the phone (its spreadsheet library flaw is an existing finding).
No join code or gym page link is used here. The four gym calls send the member's own long secret key, which the server looks up by its hash; shared-routine links live in a file outside this area.

Of the outside libraries this area uses, only the spreadsheet library (Hevy and Strong import) has dependency-scan alerts, already an existing finding; the photo, file and image libraries have none. Dependency alerts being off on the repo is also an existing finding.
